findings: Across three batches, 53 uploads represent 37 distinct files. The 16 third-batch files are new; earlier repeated uploads were byte-identical. All workbook sheets were inspected and key report methods/tables reviewed from full-text extraction (363 PDF pages).
The current Exercise Book contains 64 exercises. Some slide exercise references are offset; the pathway uses the current book numbering.
Topic 1 percentile convention and Excel QUARTILE.INC use different definitions. A numerical difference need not be a calculation error.
Topic 3 uses a rounded population variance of 9.8 for the five-unit example; exact calculation gives 9.76. Exact with-replacement mean variance is 4.88.
Adjusted sample variance is unbiased under independent sampling, but its square root (sample SD) is generally not unbiased for population SD.
Source statements differ at the n=120 boundary for the large-sample z approximation. A t reference remains suitable for an unknown-variance normal model.
Exercise 50 uses 366/589≈0.6214; the supplied solution contains inconsistent proportion/denominator values. Check the stated numerator and sample size before calculating.
Exercise 58 states 99% significance in the prompt but the supplied solution uses 1%. Clarify the intended significance level with the teacher.
The exercise 61 solution contains an inconsistent reported statistic: dividing its stated difference by its stated SE does not give the printed statistic.
Mock Q9 contains a hypothesis-label typo and slightly different CI endpoints between calculation and prose. Its original dataset was not supplied, so row-level results cannot be checked.
Topic 6 is additional, time permitting. Pooled equal-variance, paired and two-proportion formula variations on slides 15–23 are illustrative and not required for calculation according to the slides.
The statistical-table PDF includes chi-square and F tables as well as normal and t tables. Their presence alone does not add them to the assessed syllabus.
All six topic slide decks are now supplied: 274 slides in total. The complete mock paper and referenced lab/research files listed below remain outstanding.

Topic 5 slide 35 suggests using a proportion confidence interval for the test. The usual Wald interval and null-based proportion test use different SEs and need not agree exactly; the guide includes an original numerical counterexample.
Topic 5 slides 32 and 36 reference older exercise ranges (50–55 and 56–59). The uploaded 2026/27 book places Topic 5 exercises at 51–60; use the current book numbering.
Topic 5 slide 29 displays the t(64) two-sided p-value for t=2.1 as 0.04. Its unrounded value is approximately 0.03968; make decisions before rounding.

OECD: raw country values match the Answers sheet after reordering. Variables have different nonmissing counts. Sheet1!B42 reverses its upper/lower conditions and includes summary rows; its cached result is #DIV/0!.

OECD CHILDVACCIN: the stated QUARTILE.INC fences flag Mexico as well as Brazil and Argentina. A variable-specific exclusion of all three gives n=35, mean=94.9057%; the supplied filtered workbook retains Mexico and the Word table differs. The lab guide documents the discrepancy rather than treating that table as an independent answer key.
Food: all 50 rows, including numerical zeros, enter the checks. Unknown-σ 90% mean intervals use adjusted SD, SE=s/√50 and t(.95,49)=1.6765509. Total expenditure VAR.S=2603.2557 £².
The cholesterol measurements_example workbook is distinct from CHOLESTEROL.xlsx: its two n=5 samples both have mean 200 but different variances. Their pairing/independence design is not stated.
NHSR 211 reports weighted visits (not unique people); NHSR 209 uses complex-survey Korn–Graubard intervals. Keep their published intervals and denominators.

PISA Table B.1.2 includes a dependent Quebec−Canada contrast with its own SE. Appendix A flags possible student nonresponse bias. OECD 2025 uses Tukey family-wise difference intervals; neither report supports causal claims from group associations.
